transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-07-01
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 47 mins (approx)
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Tom Hargreaves (Helios CTO), Maya Kaur (Helios ML Eng), Jordan Lee (Helios Infra), Sofia (Helios PM)

Auto-summary (auto): quick performance readout for week 3 of quant POC; discussed mixed INT8/FP8 blend, fallback thresholds, KV caching differences on Helios private infra; next steps include on-prem benchmarks and tuned configs + security paperwork.

Topics:
- Week 3 results: latency & throughput deltas
- Quality impact: SNR / sample regressions
- Fallback strategy (rollout criteria)
- Infra quirks on Helios private nodes
- Next steps and ownership

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick roll call — Alex here, Priya from our engineering team is with me.
[00:10] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all, Priya. Good to see you.
[00:13] Tom (Helios CTO): Tom here. Maya, Jordan, Sofia — you on?
[00:17] Maya (Helios ML Eng): Yep, Maya. Sorry for the late ping, had a kernel update.
[00:21] Jordan (Infra): Jordan, all good.
[00:23] Sofia (Product): Sofia.
[00:25] Alex: Cool. Today is mostly a readout from the mixed-precision runs we shipped on Monday — INT8 primary with FP8 rescue for corner cases, plus a quick convo about fallback thresholds. Priya do you want to start with the perf bullets?
[00:35] Priya: Sure. So high level — across the 5k sample harness we ran last night on a snapshot of Helios' dev cluster we saw median token latency go from about 210ms in FP16 baseline to roughly 165ms in the INT8 blend. P95 moved from ~420ms down to ~330ms. That's roughly a 20-25% improvement depending on the sequence distribution. Throughput improved ~28% on steady-state for the batch sizes you're running, which I think were 8 and 16?
[00:58] Tom: Right, prod-ish batch is usually 8, sometimes 16 for batched precompute. Those numbers look promising. Any change in memory pressure? Jordan might have noticed GPU OOMs?
[01:10] Jordan: Memory reduced — about 35% less model memory used on average, which lets us fit an extra model per node. We saw one transient OOM during a long-context run where the KV cache warmed up — that was before we applied the warmup passes.
[01:23] Priya: Yeah, the warmup passes matter. We saw the first epoch of requests had higher tail latency until KV cache hit rate increased. We recommended a 3-request warmup for the private nodes.
[01:33] Maya: Can you clarify warmup — is that a client-side priming pass? We're thinking of pre-warming on our side but worried it adds cost.
[01:40] Priya: It's lightweight — send a short prompt sequence to populate KV and key prefix cache; it's a tiny cost but it avoids that cold-run p95 spike. We can automate as part of the rollout.
[01:50] Alex: Quick interjection — on the quality side, any notable deltas? Maya?
[01:55] Maya: We ran the automated eval set (RAG retrieval + open Q/A flows). The accuracy delta for question answering tasks was small — macro accuracy dropped by ~0.8 percentage points in pure INT8 compared to FP16. In the blend where we rescue to FP8 for low-confidence outputs the delta is within noise, about -0.2 to +0.1 depending on metric.
[02:18] Priya: To add — rescue heuristics are based on token-level entropy and SNR proxy. If the model output crosses the configured threshold we re-run that request on FP8 or FP16 depending on policy. That cost tradeoff is important — rescues are expensive but rare in our sample (around 6-9% of requests).
[02:35] Jordan: 6-9% rescue rate seems okay. How does the fallback latency add up, e.g., end-to-end for a rescued request?
[02:42] Priya: There's an additional 120-180ms for a rescue because we re-queue and run on the heavier variant, so it's a clear tail hit but overall P95 still better than baseline because rescues are low percent.
[02:53] Tom: Hmm. For some user flows we can't tolerate a 180ms secondary hit; we need deterministic SLA. Could we queue-rescue in background and serve a provisional response?
[03:03] Alex: That's an interesting UX pattern — deliver provisional + async upgrade. We don't have that out-of-the-box but it's feasible. Might be product work.
[03:10] Maya: For our SLAs, we'd prefer deterministic p95 for critical endpoints. Are there other options besides rescues? Like per-route pinning to FP8/FP16?
[03:19] Priya: Yes, you can pin routes to run always on FP8 or FP16. We recommend pinning high-criticality routes to FP16 (or FP8 if you validated quality) and low-criticality to INT8. Also can set a rate limit of rescues to prevent bursts.
[03:31] Sofia: Quick question — how often did you see hallucinations or semantic regressions in INT8? We flagged some earlier.
[03:38] Maya: Good callout. We saw two types: subtle truncation artifacts on long sequences, and occasional token-level substitutions affecting named entities. Not huge, but present. That's where the rescue heuristics kicked in and fixed about 70% of those cases in our sample.
[03:50] Priya: Also worth noting the composition of the eval set matters — your retrieval-heavy prompts stress the embedding head, which is sensitive. Our recommendation was config-level per-route thresholds tuned on your labeled dev set.
[04:02] Alex: Okay. Infra note — Jordan, were there any platform-specific issues we should know about?
[04:07] Jordan: One small thing: the private cluster uses older CUDA drivers on two nodes; INT8 kernels fell back to a slower path there. We recommended either driver update or pinning those nodes out of the GPU pool. We can share the kube node list.
[04:20] Priya: Ah yes, the kernel selection logic will choose fallbacks if driver/hardware doesn't support optimized kernels. That can show degraded perf on heterogeneous clusters.
[04:29] Tom: We'll patch drivers next week. Another question — pricing. If rescues happen 6-9% of the time, what's the estimated cost delta?
[04:37] Alex: For blended runs, unit cost dropped ~18% overall in our cost model, even accounting for rescues. But there's nuance if you run heavy rescue rates — cost delta reduces. I'll send a short commercial note with a couple of scenarios.
[04:50] Maya: Please include dedicated vs hosted delta. We're trying to justify reserved nodes vs hosted.
[04:55] Alex: Yep, I will.
[04:57] [05:00] Priya: Another small empirical finding — prefix caching (we call it KV prefix) gave an outsized improvement for your dataset due to repetitive instruction format. With prefix cached the token compute drops further, and rescue rates actually fall by ~1.5 points. If you enable aggressive prefix caching you'll see even better tail numbers.
[05:18] Jordan: That might help. Any changes required on our side for caching?
[05:22] Priya: Just expose the same session ID and allow us to keep prefix slots. We have a doc for implementation details — I'll drop the snippet.
[05:28] Tom: Security/reg compliance — can you re-share the SOC2 link and the audit logs format? Legal pinged us about retention settings.
[05:34] Alex: Absolutely. I'll send the SOC2 attestation and the audit log schema. For Private we can support customer-managed KMS; Jordan, you flagged HSM integration last week?
[05:43] Jordan: Yes, we want HSM for key wrapping. Is there a known pattern for Redwood Private?
[05:48] Priya: We have an HSM/KMS integration guide — includes key wrapping + node-level secrets. I'll include that in the notes.
[05:56] Maya: Back to quality — could we get more granular logs for the rescues so we can triage exactly which tokens triggered it?
[06:03] Priya: Yes, we can emit a rescue trace with token entropy and the pre/post outputs (redacted). That can be directed to your S3 or internal logging. We'll keep PII redaction in place.
[06:14] Sofia: Who will own the triage? Maya and Redwood?
[06:18] Alex: Suggested joint triage: Maya leads labeling and examples; Priya will provide interpretability traces. We can sync weekly.
[06:25] Tom: OK. Any blockers for the next run?
[06:28] Jordan: Drivers on two nodes, will patch by 2026-07-02. Also need the mixed-precision config file from Redwood so we can run on our staging pool.
[06:36] Priya: I'll send the config today with a comment block explaining thresholds.
[06:39] Alex: Great. Quick recap — we've got performance wins with INT8 blend, small quality delta that is mostly mitigated by FP8 rescue and prefix caching, infra driver issue to patch, action items assigned. Anything else?
[06:50] Maya: One ask — can we get a short script to reproduce the 5k harness locally? That helps our CI.
[06:56] Priya: Yep, I'll attach a reproducible harness script and Dockerfile.
[07:00] Alex: Cool. Before we close, one open product idea — background rescue / provisional response pattern to avoid visible tail spikes. Priya, is that something low lift?
[07:08] Priya: It's medium effort. We need a response orchestration layer and application-level flags. We can prototype but it'll take a couple sprints.
[07:15] Tom: Put it on the roadmap but not blocking POC.
[07:18] Alex: Awesome. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the config, SOC2 link, harness, and commercial note.
[07:26] Maya: Thanks.
[07:28] Jordan: Thanks.
[07:29] Sofia: Thanks all.

Meeting close.
